name: alsonpr/Henley-Passport-Index-Dataset
what_it_holds: Python scraper + structured CSV output built from the Henley Passport Index API (18 stars, updated 13 Jul 2026); converts Henley's ranking/visa-free-count data per country into CSV.
why_useful: Henley Passport Index ranks countries by visa-free destination count; as a time series (if run repeatedly) it is a slow macro proxy for outbound travel friction by nationality, marginal relevance to cross-border demand splits (gap #7).

name: hardikgw/cbp-wait-times
what_it_holds: Old (last commit 2016) app/pipeline that indexes CBP (US Customs and Border Protection) land-port and airport wait times into Elasticsearch. Contains app/ and conf/ directories (pipeline code), not a static committed dataset -- CBP publishes live wait times via bwt.cbp.gov XML feed which this scrapes/indexes.
why_useful: Demonstrates a working method to pull CBP border wait-time data (a real-time congestion/traffic proxy for land-border crossing volume, relevant to gap #10 border crossings), but the code is stale (2016) and would need rewriting against the current CBP feed; no historical data is stored in the repo itself.
themes: Cross-border and visa data: Schengen visa statistics, ESTA, ETIAS, CBP wait times, passport index, border crossings BTS

name: national-parks-bi
what_it_holds: national_parks_clean.csv with 18,851 monthly visitation records across 63 US National Parks, Jan 2000-Dec 2024 (300 months), star-schema with parks/dates dimension tables and a monthly visitation fact table, backed by a SQLite DB with ETL staging layer. Source stated as NPS Public Use Statistics Office (irma.nps.gov/Stats).
why_useful: Long, clean, monthly, government-sourced NPS visitation series across 63 parks (24 years) is a ready-made national-scale US leisure-travel/destination-demand proxy that could nowcast domestic NA nights alongside TSA throughput; addresses destination-demand gap adjacent to gap 10 (travel volume) and general consumer/travel strength gaps.
themes: Destination demand proxies: US National Park Service visitation stats API, state park attendance, museum/theme-park attendance, ski resort data, beach visitation
why_all: Long, clean, monthly, government-sourced NPS visitation series across 63 parks (24 years) is a ready-made national-scale US leisure-travel/destination-demand proxy that could nowcast domestic NA nights alongside TSA throughput; addresses destination-demand gap adjacent to gap 10 (travel volume) and general consumer/travel strength gaps.

name: FIFA-World-Cup-2026-Dataset
what_it_holds: 12 committed CSVs: venues.csv (16 stadiums, city/country/capacity/lat-lon across US/Canada/Mexico), matches.csv + matches_detailed.csv (104 matches, date, kickoff_time_utc, stage, venue_id, teams, scores, xG), teams.csv (48 teams, group, FIFA rank/Elo), squads_and_players.csv (1,248 players), plus match_events, match_team_stats, match_lineups, player_stats, match_prediction_features (65 ML features). Actively updated during the tournament (Jun 11-Jul 19 2026). CC0-1.0 license, 63 stars, updated 30 Aug 2026.
why_useful: Directly fills gap #11 (World Cup 2026 host-city/schedule data): venue city + exact match date lets us build a host-city demand-shock calendar for 3Q26 nights/ADR (World Cup falls entirely inside 3Q26). Capacity and lat/lon support a per-market intensity weight (e.g. more matches/bigger stadium in a metro = larger STR demand pulse) for NA markets in the Inside Airbnb panel.
